title: Boss: the certificate workshop
summary: Signatures, self-signed certificates, fields and PEM, all in one go.

steps.title: The workshop
body: Four jobs, each a little harder. You will need:
The namespaces are imported in every step.

steps.title: Who signed it?
prompt: You have a message, its signature, and a list of public keys from several people.
Write `int WhoSigned(string message, byte[] signature, List<ECDsa> keys)` that returns the index of the key that
verifies the signature (UTF-8, SHA-256), or `-1` if none does.
starter: int WhoSigned(string message, byte[] signature, List<ECDsa> keys)
solution: int WhoSigned(string message, byte[] signature, List<ECDsa> keys)
hints: Loop over the keys and call `VerifyData` on each.
Return the index of the first success.
template: Dojo.Eq("key 2 signed \"release v2\"", 2, WhoSigned("release v2", dojoSig, dojoKeys));
Dojo.Eq("nobody signed \"release v3\" with that signature", -1, WhoSigned("release v3", dojoSig, dojoKeys));
Dojo.Eq("empty key list gives -1", -1, WhoSigned("release v2", dojoSig, new List<ECDsa>()));

steps.title: A proper dev certificate
prompt: Write `X509Certificate2 MakeDevCert()` that returns a self-signed certificate (with its private key) for local HTTPS:
- Subject `CN=dojo.local`, ECDSA P-256, SHA-256
- valid from 2030-01-01 to 2031-01-01 UTC
- Basic Constraints: **not** a CA, critical
- SAN: DNS names `dojo.local` and `localhost`
- EKU: server authentication, OID `1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1`
Add extensions with `req.CertificateExtensions.Add(...)` before calling `CreateSelfSigned`.
starter: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=dojo.local", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
// add the extensions, then create the certificate
solution: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=dojo.local", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
hints: `new X509BasicConstraintsExtension(false, false, 0, true)`: not a CA, no path length limit, critical.
template: Dojo.Eq("Has its private key", true, dojoC.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Check("Basic Constraints present, not a CA, critical", dojoBc != null && !dojoBc.CertificateAuthority && dojoBc.Critical, "check the X509BasicConstraintsExtension arguments");
Dojo.Eq("SAN DNS names", new List<string> { "dojo.local", "localhost" }, dojoSan == null ? new List<string>() : dojoSan.EnumerateDnsNames().ToList());

Dojo.Check("EKU contains serverAuth", dojoEku != null && dojoEku.EnhancedKeyUsages.Cast<Oid>().Any(o => o.Value == "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1"), "add an X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension with 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1");

steps.title: Summarise a PEM
prompt: A teammate pastes a PEM certificate into chat. Write `string Summary(string pem)` that loads it with
`X509Certificate2.CreateFromPem(pem)` and returns one line:
```text
CN=shop.example | issued by CN=Test Root | CA: False | DNS: shop.example, www.shop.example
- `CA:` is `True` only if Basic Constraints exists and says CA.
- `DNS:` lists the SAN DNS names joined with `, `; if there is no SAN, write `DNS: none`.
solution: var names = san == null ? new List<string>() : san.EnumerateDnsNames().ToList();
hints: Reuse the ideas from *Inspect a certificate*: `OfType<...>().FirstOrDefault()`.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Test Root", null, true);
Dojo.Eq("leaf summary", "CN=shop.example | issued by CN=Test Root | CA: False | DNS: shop.example, www.shop.example", Summary(dojoLeaf.ExportCertificatePem()));
Dojo.Eq("root summary", "CN=Test Root | issued by CN=Test Root | CA: True | DNS: none", Summary(dojoRoot.ExportCertificatePem()));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Survive the round trip
prompt: Prove that a PEM copy of a certificate is the same certificate, and that the copy cannot sign.
Write `bool SameCertificate(X509Certificate2 original)` that:
1. exports `original` to PEM and loads it back with `X509Certificate2.CreateFromPem`,
2. returns true only if the copy's `RawData` equals the original's byte for byte (`SequenceEqual`),
the `Thumbprint`s are equal, **and** the copy has **no** private key.
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Round Trip Root", null, true);
Dojo.Check("original has a private key (test setup)", dojoRoot.HasPrivateKey, "setup");
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
steps.explain: PEM and DER carry exactly the same bytes, so the thumbprint survives. The private key never travels with a certificate export; only a PFX (or a separate key file) carries it.
